title: security: RBAC v2 enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Maya Tran
description:
Motivation: finalize RBAC v2 KMS region pinning enforcement and harden audit logs to include KMS key metadata and residency flags. Customers in regulated environments require verifiable records that a request was pinned to a customer-approved KMS region and which key was used. This PR turns the previous audit-only mode into an enforceable policy behind a feature flag, adds migration tooling, and improves end-to-end coverage.

What changed (summary):
- Add enforcement checks to RBAC v2 policy evaluator for kms_region pinning (enforce or audit-only).
- Augment audit logging to capture kms_key_id, kms_region, residency_policy_id, and decision_reason for denials.
- Feature flag: security.kms.region_pin.enforce (default: false for safety).
- Migration: DB migration to populate existing resources with policy_digest and residency metadata.
- E2E tests and unit tests covering allow/deny flows, fallback behavior, and audit-only -> enforce cutover.
- Docs: updated security and private deployment docs with guidance and rollout steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Add policy evaluator changes and unit tests
- [x] Add audit log fields and wire to observability pipeline
- [x] Implement migration script and smoke test
- [x] Update docs and release notes
- [x] Run canary in staging and validated with dedicated capacity

Compatibility/behavior notes:
- Default is audit-only. Enabling enforcement requires a migration and an operator-initiated feature flag flip. See docs for safe rollout steps.
- When enforcement is enabled, requests that do not meet kms_region pinning will be denied with clear decision_reason = "kms_region_pinning_violation" and will be logged.

Backwards-incompatible changes:
- This PR adds a potential denial path when enforcement is enabled. Customers must follow migration steps before flipping the flag. Marking as a potential breaking change in release notes.
